executive_summary: EUR/CHF trades at 0.93892 as of the 2026-09-03 close from the gated price store, two sessions after the 2026-09-01 valuation date, and the pair has risen 0.68% over one month, 2.03% over three months, 4.04% over six months and 0.69% over twelve — a flat year that conceals a fall to 0.9025 in early March and a 4% recovery since. On a closing basis spot sits at the 92nd percentile of its 52-week 0.90152–0.94211 range, and the intraday 52-week high of 0.94391 was set on 2 September, one session before the payload close. The dominant bilateral narrative is a policy differential of +225bp — an ECB at a 2.25% deposit rate against an SNB policy rate of 0.00% — that is scheduled to widen to 250bp on 10 September against a quote-leg central bank whose own three-year conditional inflation forecast is explicitly conditioned on staying at zero, and the market has noticed: the franc's growing use as a funding currency in place of the yen is pushing EUR/CHF higher, with carry traders turning to a European rather than an Asian funding leg. The bilateral fact that diverges most sharply from the two standalone dossiers is the external balance: the euro area's current-account surplus has fallen to 1.7% of GDP while Switzerland runs 9.77% off a CHF 974bn net international investment position, an eight-point gap that neither dossier frames as a pair constraint but which, at an 0.18 strategic weight, cancels the entire rate advantage. The second is convexity — the pair's estimated three-month implied volatility of 3.457% is a documented floor on a cross whose central bank moved it roughly 30% intraday in January 2015, and it charges nothing for an ECB projections round, an SNB assessment and a Swiss constitutional referendum falling inside eighteen days. The settled verdict is tactically Bullish at conviction 3 (net weighted score +0.3705) and strategically Neutral at conviction 2 (−0.0279), and this pass concurs on direction while noting the honest caveat that most of the tactical score is scheduled rather than discovered: at a 97%-priced hike and a fully-priced hold, the pair is being paid by 273.4bp of annualised carry accrual and regime persistence, not by new information, into a five-touch resistance band that has already rejected it three times in three weeks.

market_context.valuation_assessment: There is no pair-level PPP series for EUR/CHF, so the comparison is made through relative BIS real effective exchange rates for June 2026 (cache-sourced, ~92 days old): euro area real broad effective rate 102.69, down 1.20 points over twelve months; Switzerland 101.69, down 1.03 points. The euro is roughly 1.0% richer than the franc in real effective terms, close to parity, meaning a 225bp policy gap about to become 250bp has bought the euro essentially nothing in real trade-weighted terms. Both currencies sit mid-distribution (euro estimated 45th percentile, franc estimated 40th on a 30-month window, both estimates). A 92nd closing percentile in the nominal 52-week range against a ~1% real effective differential says the market has monetised the policy gap in spot while the real exchange rate has not moved — a carry-consistent structure rather than a mispricing. BNY's Geoff Yu has argued the franc looks undervalued on both nominal and real effective measures, near one-year and 15-month lows respectively, a direct counterpoint worth carrying. Valuation offers no mean-reversion urgency inside four weeks and only a weak, franc-favouring pull over one to six months, consistent with the strategic Neutral.

market_context.recent_regime: The last thirty sessions describe a grind higher punctuated by three rejections at the same ceiling. From 0.93090 on 31 July the pair advanced almost without interruption to 0.94107 on 14 August, held 0.94047 on 18 August, then reversed violently on 19 August — a 97-pip down day at roughly 2.5x ATR, the largest single-session decline in the window. It rebuilt to 0.93758 by 28 August, pushed to a new closing high of 0.94211 on 2 September with an intraday 0.94391 52-week high, before failing again on 3 September to close at 0.93892. Three attempts at 0.9408–0.9439 in three weeks, each rejected, with the higher-low structure intact throughout. The narrative is carry-trade driven — EUR/CHF pushing to new 2026 highs was read as a signal that investors continue to fund in the lowest-yielding currencies while markets remain calm — countered by a 14 August Swiss Q2 GDP print of +1.5% against a 0.2-0.4% consensus, which triggered the 19 August reversal.

bilateral_carry_analysis.carry_assessment: The annualised carry on a long EUR/CHF position is +273.4bp, taken from the CME calendar-spread cross (6S/6E, 6SU6→6SZ6) observed 2026-08-31. By covered interest parity this is the interest differential plus the cross-currency basis; the ~48bp by which it exceeds the +225bp policy differential is reported as residual basis rather than attributed to either component. Against the estimated 3M ATM implied volatility of 3.457% the carry-to-vol ratio is 0.79 (an upper bound given the implied figure is a documented floor); against 60-day realised volatility of 3.90% it is 0.70. Either figure is the best risk-adjusted carry available anywhere in the euro complex — ahead of EUR/JPY at +0.19 and EUR/SEK at +0.11, with every other euro cross negative. Carry is working and this pair is the cleanest expression of it: a zero-rate quote leg whose central bank has published a three-year commitment to zero, against a base leg that is actively tightening, in a benign risk tape (VIX 14.51, US HY 263bp), is the textbook funding-currency short. The regime's dependency is realised volatility, not direction — at 4.82% 20-day realised the carry is comfortably economic, but a sustained move above 8% would make it marginal within weeks.

factors.weight_adjustment_reason: Weight raised +0.03 at both horizons. On a cross with an anchored zero-rate quote leg, the rate channel is a larger share of the total signal than the default weight assumes.

tactical.bilateral_analysis: The bilateral differential is +225bp in the euro's favour: an ECB deposit facility rate of 2.25% against an SNB policy rate of 0.00%, the widest positive carry available to a long-euro position anywhere in the G10. It is also the only euro differential scheduled to widen inside the tactical window. The 10 September Governing Council is a projections round and is priced at roughly 97% for 25bp, which would take the spread to 250bp; the 24 September SNB assessment is a near-certain hold because the June conditional inflation forecast of 0.6% for 2026, 0.6% for 2027 and 0.7% for 2028 is explicitly conditioned on a 0% policy rate across the entire three-year horizon. The 10-year Bund-Confederation spread of 266bp, on a consistent 2026-06-01 monthly basis, is already 41bp wider than the policy gap, so the term structure prices euro-area tightening beyond the front end rather than merely matching it. Transmission is carry rather than repricing: the CME calendar-spread cross puts the annualised roll on a long EUR/CHF position at 273.4bp, about 48bp above the policy differential, with the residual being cross-currency basis that cannot be separated without an OIS curve. The honest qualification is that the September decision is discounted; what remains genuinely two-sided is the terminal, and that resolves after this horizon.

strategic.bilateral_analysis: Over one to three months the differential's level stays overwhelmingly in the euro's favour but its second derivative turns. The euro leg travels from 2.25% to a priced 2.50% on 10 September, with a live but non-consensus 2.75% available at the 17 December projections round; the franc leg cannot move, because the SNB conditions its own three-year forecast on zero and Chairman Schlegel has repeatedly cited the undesirable side effects of negative rates, so the distribution around 0.00% is tight and near-symmetric. That asymmetry means the strategic rate case for the pair is unusually robust to franc-side surprise and depends almost entirely on the euro leg. The problem is that the euro leg's impulse is imported: euro-area core HICP is 2.5% against a headline heading for 3.3% on energy, the ECB's own negotiated wage tracker printed 2.1% for Q2 2026 against 3.2% in 2025, and Brent has already fallen from 100.31 on 24 July to 88.24 on 25 August. If the ECB stops after September, a static 250bp spread stops generating fresh divergence and becomes a carry level rather than a directional force — still supportive of the pair, but by accrual rather than by repricing. The dated tests are 29 October, which is not a projections round and is therefore the language meeting, and 17 December, which is.

tactical.bilateral_analysis: The inflation differential and the growth differential point in opposite directions, and for this pair the inflation differential wins because it is the only one that reaches a policy rate. Euro-area HICP ran 2.9% in July with core at 2.5% and services at 3.3%, and the August flash consensus was 3.3% headline; Swiss headline CPI eased to 0.4% with core at 0.3% and goods deflation deepening. That is a bilateral inflation gap of roughly 2.5 percentage points, and it is the entire reason one central bank is hiking and the other is pinned. Growth runs the other way and runs hard: SECO's Q2 flash put Swiss GDP at +1.5% quarter-on-quarter against a 0.2-0.4% consensus, the KOF barometer printed 106.7 in August, its highest since November 2021, and Swiss industrial production beat by more than ten points. Euro-area Q2 GDP was +0.4% quarter-on-quarter with German Ifo at 88.8 against 87.2 expected. So Switzerland is winning the surprise contest on activity and losing it decisively on prices. Transmission is asymmetric: a Swiss growth beat cannot move an SNB whose CPI is 0.4%, whereas a euro-area inflation beat feeds directly into a decision six days later. Bilateral sensitivity therefore sits with the euro-area price data, not the Swiss activity data.

strategic.bilateral_analysis: Over one to three months both legs of the differential decay, and they decay towards each other. The euro-area overshoot is imported cost-push, not domestic demand-pull: energy contributed 0.94pp of the July headline at +10.0% year-on-year while food, processed food and non-energy industrial goods all decelerated, and the ECB's own wage tracker at 2.1% cannot sustain 3.3% services inflation. The Eurosystem's June projections have headline back at 2.0% in 2028. On the Swiss side the growth strength is very probably borrowed: US Section 232 pharmaceutical tariffs of up to 15% were announced on 2 April and took effect on 31 July, July chemical and pharmaceutical exports jumped 25.7%, and exports pulled forward are exports that will not recur — the IMF's 0.8% for 2026 and the SNB's around 1% both sit far below a 1.5% quarterly run rate. So the euro's inflation advantage narrows and Switzerland's growth advantage narrows at the same time. Neither leg produces a durable directional signal for the pair, and the level of Swiss inflation is too low either to threaten the SNB's zero or to open a deflationary case for going below it. Neutral is the honest reading rather than a refusal to choose.

factors.horizon_split: Bullish tactically and Neutral strategically at identical confidence, because the horizon changes which half of the differential is doing the work. Over four weeks the pair is paid for the LEVEL of the inflation gap and for the direction of euro-area price surprises, both of which feed a decision on 10 September. Over one to three months it would need PERSISTENCE, and persistence requires euro-area wages, which at 2.1% are not there — while Swiss growth strength simultaneously unwinds as pharmaceutical front-running reverses.

tactical.bilateral_analysis: EUR/CHF is a moderate-beta risk pair with a clean directional interpretation: the franc is a haven and the euro is not, so risk-on lifts the pair and risk-off drops it. The current cross-asset configuration is close to the ideal for the pair. VIX closed at 14.51 on 27 August, down 3.70 points on the month after touching a 2026 low of 14.2; US investment-grade spreads are 79bp and high yield 263bp, 21bp tighter on the month; the Euro Stoxx 50 set an all-time high above 6,560 and the DAX broke 26,450 for the first time. European equity leadership matters more for this pair than for most, because it is a portfolio-inflow channel that runs into euro assets specifically rather than into the dollar. The single dissenting signal is gold, which at 4,456.44 is up 8.60% on the month and 22.39% on the year: the franc's traditional correlate is being bought hard while the franc is sold, which is a correlation breakdown rather than confirmation, and it says the haven bid has been rerouted rather than extinguished. Over four weeks the prevailing regime is the signal and the regime is unambiguously pair-positive; the caveat is that this is the factor most capable of reversing without notice, with an active Gulf conflict inside the window.

strategic.bilateral_analysis: Over one to three months the risk factor stops being a directional read on the pair and becomes a statement about the shape of the distribution, and from VIX 14.51 with high yield at 263bp that distribution is one-sided. Both measures are near the tight end of their post-2022 ranges, so there is far more room for volatility to rise than to compress further, and the pair's payoff to rising volatility is negative and convex: a genuine risk-off episode simultaneously bids the franc as a haven and hits the euro as a non-haven with an energy-import problem, so both legs move the same way against the pair. The identifiable catalysts are not hypothetical — an unresolved Gulf conflict that has already produced a 12% Brent round trip, a European winter gas balance against 62.99% storage, and a French 2027 budget process. Against that, the constructive case is real: record European equities reflecting fiscal and earnings optimism, a German infrastructure and defence programme providing a multi-year demand floor, and portfolio inflows into European assets that historically accompany euro strength. The two forces are close to balanced over the horizon, which is why the honest stance is Neutral rather than Bearish — the pair does not need risk appetite to improve from here, but it cannot rely on it either.

tactical.bilateral_analysis: Speculators are short the base currency AND short the quote currency, which is the configuration that mutes a pair signal rather than amplifying it. The euro non-commercial net was -36,352 contracts at the 25 August report, having covered 22,736 in a single week from -59,088; the franc all-speculator net was -19.9k at the 28 August release, having covered from -32.5k on 14 August. The internal structures differ in a way that matters bilaterally: euro open interest is 801,884 contracts with asset managers long 225,389 against leveraged funds short 60,600, whereas franc open interest is only 109,874 with asset managers short 38,322 against dealers long 62,382. So the quote leg's short is concentrated in slow-moving real money on a shallow contract, while the base leg's short is fast money on the deepest FX futures market in the world. The squeeze that would have moved this pair has already been taken on both sides, which is why the tactical stance is Neutral rather than directional.

strategic.bilateral_analysis: Over one to three months the two legs' positioning arguments are individually strong and bilaterally cancelling. On the base side, a residual -36,352 euro short against a differential that improves versus seven of ten peers is a genuine asymmetry: converting it to even a modest net long would represent roughly 86,000 contracts, about USD 12.5bn of notional demand. On the quote side, a -38,322 asset-manager franc short on only 109,874 contracts of open interest is the classic squeeze fuel that has produced every violent franc rally in the record, and it moves against the pair. Netted, the strategic flow picture is close to flat with a fat and identifiable left tail: the franc leg squeezes faster than the euro leg converts, because real-money positions on a shallow contract unwind in days while euro positioning shifts take months to move price against 800,000 contracts of open interest. Two structural qualifications cut the same way. The euro's share of allocated global reserves fell to 20.03% in Q1 2026 from 20.38%, so the official bid on the base leg is running in reverse; and the SNB holds roughly CHF 890bn of official reserve assets and has stated an increased willingness to intervene against franc appreciation, which caps the magnitude of any squeeze without changing its direction.

Strategically the individual asymmetries become large but remain opposed — the base leg has room to convert to a long over months, the quote leg has fuel to squeeze in days — and the correct bilateral reading of two opposed asymmetries with different clocks is a Neutral with an explicitly stated left tail, not a manufactured direction.

tactical.combined_positioning_signal: Short base and short quote simultaneously, both near the midpoint of their one-year bands: the implied pair position is roughly flat and carries no contrarian trigger. The euro leg cut 38% of its aggregate short in the week to 25 August and the franc leg cut roughly 40% over three weeks to 28 August, so the covering that would have driven a squeeze in either direction is in the past tense.
tactical.unwind_trigger: A pair-level unwind now requires an exogenous shock rather than positional pressure. The credible four-week candidates are a Gulf re-escalation that reverses Brent's fall and pushes VIX above 20, an SNB assessment on 24 September that drops the intervention language and is read as tolerance of a stronger franc, or a euro-area flash HICP undershoot that puts the 10 September hike back in question.
tactical.historical_analogue: Franc squeezes from a comparably one-sided real-money book have been violent rather than orderly — the January 2015 floor removal moved this pair roughly 30% intraday — but from a -19.9k aggregate the fast-money component that must move quickly is only about 11,400 contracts, so a squeeze from here would be moderate by that standard.
tactical.contrarian_case: The genuine contrarian observation runs against the tactical Bullish verdict on this pair: with the base-leg hike discounted at 97%, the quote-leg hold discounted at close to certainty, and speculative covering complete on both sides, the marginal buyer of EUR/CHF on 10 September has to be motivated by something other than positioning or policy news — and inside the tactical window there is no obvious candidate beyond carry accrual itself.

strategic.combined_positioning_signal: Two large opposed asymmetries on different clocks. A residual euro short worth roughly USD 12.5bn of latent demand if it converts, against a concentrated franc real-money short worth roughly 49,754 contracts of forced buying on a contract one-seventh the depth. Net pair implication is flat with a left tail.
strategic.unwind_trigger: The quote leg unwinds on any risk event that revives haven demand: a Hormuz closure sustained through winter, European credit stress as the ECB tightens into an energy shock, or a French budget accident that widens OAT-Bund beyond 120bp. The base leg converts only slowly and only on delivered policy — a second ECB hike at the 17 December projections round is the cleanest trigger.
strategic.historical_analogue: Euro positioning squeezes deliver three-to-five percent over months because 800,000 contracts of open interest absorb enormous flow before price moves; franc squeezes deliver comparable moves in days. The 2015 episode is the extreme, and the SNB's roughly CHF 890bn of reserves plus its stated intervention willingness is the dampener that did not exist in the same form then.
strategic.contrarian_case: The strategic contrarian case is that consensus is quietly short the same tail twice. Bank forecasts cluster at 0.93-0.95 through 2027 and rest on a modal path with no allowance for a haven event, while the pair's own estimated three-month implied volatility of 3.457% — itself a documented floor — charges almost nothing for a currency whose defining behaviour is a low-volatility grind punctuated by jumps. Being flat the pair and long its convexity is the position consensus is not carrying.

factors.weight_adjustment_reason: +0.02 strategically only. This is a terms-of-trade cross in the framework's own sense: the world's largest net energy importer against a twin-surplus economy running a current account near 10% of GDP, with the energy shock live and physically dated to the winter storage season.

tactical.bilateral_analysis: The external differential is the largest single fundamental negative for this pair and it is worsening. The euro area's current-account surplus has fallen to 1.7% of GDP over the twelve months to June from 2.0%, with the goods surplus down from EUR 342bn to EUR 282bn, while Switzerland ran 9.77% of GDP in Q1 2026 with a net international investment position of CHF 974bn and a July trade surplus of CHF 8.1bn, the largest since the series began in 1950. The commodity channel compounds it: Dutch TTF gas topped EUR 70/MWh on 31 August, the highest since January 2023, EU storage was 62.99% full on 24 August, and the Strait of Hormuz is effectively closed to roughly a fifth of global LNG trade. Under the framework's direction rules, gas up is strongly euro-negative and gold up is franc-positive, and gold is up 8.60% on the month — both legs push the pair down. The genuine bilateral offset runs the other way and is worth stating: IMF DOTS shows the euro area exporting USD 195.8bn of goods to Switzerland against USD 139.5bn imported, a net euro-area surplus of USD 56.3bn, which is a structural trade-flow bid for euros against francs. Over four weeks the flow news has been mildly pair-supportive while the price signal that drives the next quarter of flows is clearly pair-negative, and the price signal leads.

strategic.bilateral_analysis: At an 0.18 strategic weight this is the counterweight that neutralises the entire rate advantage, and the arithmetic behind it is slow, mechanical and high-confidence. The euro area must buy scarce LNG at the margin through the autumn in competition with Asia against 62.99% storage and a closed Hormuz, and Goldman Sachs has said explicitly that current prices will not be enough to manage storage through winter, with December TTF possibly needing to exceed EUR 100/MWh. Every EUR 10/MWh is a direct debit to a goods surplus that has already shed EUR 60bn. Switzerland faces no equivalent constraint: it is a smaller net energy importer, it gains from Brent's 12-dollar fall, and its surplus is generated by pharmaceuticals, precision engineering, financial services and a large primary income stream from a CHF 974bn net international investment position worth roughly 120% of GDP. The two offsets are genuine and both are quantifiable. Switzerland faces US Section 232 pharmaceutical tariffs of up to 15% that will reverse some of the July export surge inside this horizon, and it has committed to facilitate at least USD 200bn of US investment over five years, USD 67bn of it in 2026 — a real outbound flow against its own surplus. Netting them still leaves an 8-point current-account differential running against the pair, with a dated winter test.

Our expectation is that the euro-area twelve-month current-account ratio prints below 1.5% of GDP by the February 2027 releases, and that is the single largest gap between our view and the market's on this cross.

factors.horizon_split: Bearish at both horizons with confidence rising from 55 to 70 and the weight tripling from 0.06 to 0.18, so the strategic contribution is roughly four times the tactical one. Balance-of-payments flows are cumulative: a record Swiss trade month and a EUR 70/MWh gas print are curiosities over four weeks and a binding constraint over a quarter, once the winter import bill is multiplied by volumes. The dated inflection is the autumn injection season, which determines whether Europe enters winter near 75% or 85% storage.

net_commodity_exposure.base_commodity_profile: The euro area is the world's largest net energy importer and its critical commodity is Dutch TTF natural gas, currently above EUR 70/MWh and at a three-and-a-half-year high with storage at 62.99% and Hormuz effectively closed. It is also a net oil importer, so Brent's fall from 100.31 to 88.24 is a partial offset, and it has no meaningful commodity export to set against either.
net_commodity_exposure.quote_commodity_profile: Switzerland is a net energy importer too, but far less energy-intensive per unit of GDP, so it gains from cheaper oil without the same gas exposure. Its distinctive commodity linkage is gold: it is the world's largest refining hub and the franc's principal commodity correlate, and gold is up 8.60% on the month and 22.39% on the year. Commodity trading houses domiciled in Switzerland also contribute to the services surplus.
net_commodity_exposure.net_effect_calculation: Applying the framework's direction rules leg by leg. Natural gas up: strongly negative for the euro, mildly negative for the franc as a smaller importer — net NEGATIVE for the pair, and this is the dominant term because gas is the binding physical constraint on the euro area this winter. Oil down: mildly positive for both importers, marginally more positive for the more energy-intensive euro area — net mildly POSITIVE for the pair, and it is the only commodity term currently working in the pair's favour. Gold up: positive for the franc through both the refining channel and the haven correlation, neutral for the euro — net NEGATIVE for the pair, and gold's 8.60% monthly move makes this a live rather than theoretical term. Summing: one large negative (gas), one meaningful negative (gold), one modest positive (oil). Net commodity exposure is clearly negative for EUR/CHF, and the negativity is concentrated in exactly the commodity whose forward curve is steepening into the winter.
net_commodity_exposure.scenario_oil_up_10pct: Brent from 88.24 to roughly 97 would hurt the euro area more than Switzerland on energy intensity, and in the current configuration an oil rally would almost certainly arrive as Gulf escalation, which simultaneously bids the franc as a haven and drags gas higher. Net: clearly bearish EUR/CHF, plausibly by 1-2% on the escalation channel alone.
net_commodity_exposure.scenario_oil_down_10pct: Brent to roughly 79 improves both terms of trade, more for the euro area in proportion, and would most plausibly reflect de-escalation that also collapses TTF and removes the franc's haven bid. Net: bullish EUR/CHF, and the single cleanest way for the strategic Bearish reading on this factor to be wrong.
net_commodity_exposure.dominant_commodity_driver: Dutch TTF natural gas. It is the only commodity that hits one leg of this pair hard and the other barely at all, it has a dated physical test in the northern-hemisphere heating season against 62.99% storage, and it is the mechanism by which the euro area's goods surplus has already lost EUR 60bn.

factors.weight_adjustment_reason: +0.01 tactically only. Both central banks communicate inside the tactical window — the ECB with a projections round on 10 September and the SNB with a quarterly assessment on 24 September — and the SNB's guidance is an explicitly asymmetric statement about the exchange rate itself rather than about rates, which gives it unusually direct transmission to this specific cross.

tactical.bilateral_analysis: Guidance divergence on this pair is as one-sided as it gets in the G10. The ECB's Account of the 22-23 July meeting, published 27 August, twice described the hold as a pause, stated it was important not to signal the end of the tightening cycle, and judged a further hike likely unless the inflation outlook improved significantly — optionality-preserving hawkishness that moved pricing to roughly 97% within days. The SNB's June assessment said it has an increased willingness to intervene against a rapid and excessive appreciation of the franc, a formulation Chairman Schlegel reaffirmed on 8 July, and there is no corresponding commitment anywhere to lean against franc weakness. For a holder of this pair that is a written option: one central bank is signalling it will keep tightening, the other has said it will sell its own currency if it rallies hard and will do nothing if it falls. Credibility is high on both sides by the only test that matters, delivery — the ECB hiked in June for the first time in three years, and the SNB holds roughly CHF 890bn of reserves with the strongest FX intervention record in the developed world. Sequence matters: the ECB speaks on 10 September and sets the tone before the SNB responds on 24 September.

tactical.what_is_priced: The market has fully bought the ECB's message at roughly 97% and treats the SNB's intervention language as a permanent feature of the landscape. The unpriced risk is a change in that sentence: after a multi-month franc depreciation the pressure the language was written to counter has abated, and softening it on 24 September would be read as tolerance of a stronger franc.

strategic.bilateral_analysis: Over one to three months the guidance factor stops asking whether the market believes each bank and starts asking whether each bank's own framework can sustain what the market has extrapolated. On the base leg it cannot, quite: a 2.75% terminal by early 2027 has to be reconciled with the ECB's own wage tracker at 2.1% and its own projection of 2.0% inflation in 2028, and a downward drift in terminal pricing is pair-negative even if it is entirely orderly and well communicated. On the quote leg the guidance is durable but conditional in a way that does not help a long position: it is written to counter appreciation, so it caps the franc's upside without providing any support to the pair if the euro leg stalls. The SNB's structural incentive over the horizon is, if anything, reinforced — a 15% Section 232 pharmaceutical tariff raises its sensitivity to any further loss of competitiveness through the exchange rate — but a central bank that surprised the market by 30% in January 2015 is also the reason nobody assumes its guidance binds indefinitely. The dated tests are the 29 October ECB, which is not a projections round and is therefore the pure language meeting, and the 17 December projections round, at which energy base effects first enter the 2027-28 forecast window.

factors.horizon_split: Bullish tactically and Neutral strategically. Tactically the guidance is doing its job on both sides in the same direction — a 97%-priced hike from a bank with a clean delivery record, followed two weeks later by a bank that has publicly committed to leaning only against franc strength. Strategically the same guidance becomes the source of the risk, because the market has extrapolated the euro leg past what the ECB's own wage and inflation arithmetic supports, and the franc-side cap provides no support to the pair when that repricing arrives. The transition point is the 17 December projections round.

tactical.bilateral_analysis: Event risk on this pair is asymmetric and the asymmetry runs against it, because the dominant live event hits both legs in the same direction. A Gulf escalation raises euro-area energy costs and simultaneously revives haven demand for the franc, so the pair loses twice; the most recent news flow is escalatory, with Iran's IRGC claiming on 31 August that it downed a US MQ-9 drone over the Strait of Hormuz and attacked a UAE air base. The second one-sided negative is French: a 2027 budget must pass a fragmented parliament with record debt, Fitch affirmed A+ on 28 August with an explicit warning, and OAT-Bund at 83.6bp is elevated but priced benignly. Against those, the Swiss-specific dated item is the 27 September referendum on constitutionally entrenching neutrality, polling roughly 62-36 against on August surveys, so rejection is the base case and the modal outcome is a non-event; passage would be genuinely ambiguous for the franc, arguably enhancing the neutrality claim while adding sanctions and market-access friction. Event clustering is dense — 10 September, 24 September and 27 September inside eighteen days — and nothing in the pair's estimated volatility surface charges for it. Over four weeks the escalation branch dominates because the de-escalation branch has no dated catalyst.

strategic.bilateral_analysis: Over one to three months the event set broadens and the skew persists against the pair, though it becomes genuinely two-sided in a way worth stating honestly. The escalation branch is straightforwardly negative: a Hormuz closure through the northern winter against 62.99% storage pushes TTF towards the EUR 100/MWh Goldman has flagged, deepens the euro-area goods deterioration, and forces the ECB to tighten into a real-income squeeze while the franc collects the haven bid. The de-escalation branch is genuinely positive for the pair and is under-appreciated: a durable ceasefire collapses gas and oil, restores euro-area terms of trade, and removes the franc's haven premium at the same time — it would also end the ECB cycle, but the terms-of-trade channel is larger for the euro area than the rate channel, so the net for this cross is up. What tips the balance negative is that the remaining one-sided risks sit on the base leg: the French 2027 budget process, Ukraine financing that is growth-positive but debt-additive, and the early-February 2027 expiry of the EU's retaliatory-tariff pause. Switzerland's own strategic event set — Bilaterals III ratification, a concentrated banking system — is slower and mostly undated.

factors.horizon_split: Bearish at both horizons with identical confidence, but for different reasons. Tactically the escalation branch dominates because the latest news flow is escalatory and de-escalation has no dated catalyst inside four weeks. Strategically a durable ceasefire becomes a live possibility and would be pair-positive on both legs, which nearly cancels the escalation risk — what keeps the strategic stance negative is the one-sided base-leg political and fiscal risk running into the French 2027 budget.

tactical.bilateral_analysis: The sovereign differential clearly favours the quote leg but generates no impulse inside four weeks, which is the definition of a Neutral. Switzerland is AAA at every major agency, reconfirmed by Morningstar DBRS on 16 January 2026, with general government debt at 37.6% of GDP on the rating-agency measure — 40.7% on the IMF's and nearer 30% on a Maastricht basis, a range worth stating rather than a single number — a small structural surplus and a constitutional debt brake. The euro area has no single sovereign, so the comparison has to be made member by member: a AAA Germany borrowing heavily, an A+ France affirmed on 28 August with an explicit deficit warning, and an Italy re-rated to Baa2 after seven upgrades. Crucially, none of it is currently stressed. OAT-Bund at 83.6bp and BTP-Bund at roughly 81-85bp are elevated but orderly and nowhere near levels at which the Transmission Protection Instrument becomes a live consideration, and auctions are clearing normally across the bloc. There is no scheduled fiscal event on either side inside the tactical window capable of moving this cross more than a few pips, so the factor is a background condition that is presently benign.

strategic.bilateral_analysis: Over one to three months the factor changes from absolute to relative and turns modestly against the pair. Switzerland's fiscal position does not improve; the alternatives deteriorate, and that is the mechanism by which sovereign quality becomes an FX factor. Bund yields at a fifteen-year high reflect both the ECB cycle and a German fiscal expansion with new borrowing reported above EUR 180bn in the adopted budget plus a EUR 500bn infrastructure fund, and while higher core yields with contained peripheral spreads is historically a euro-supportive configuration, the euro area's fat left tail is now located in Paris rather than Rome. A French 2027 budget that must pass a parliament unable to pass structural reform is a higher-probability disruption than 83.6bp implies, and an OAT-Bund move beyond 110-120bp would reintroduce a fragmentation premium across the whole complex and constrain ECB hawkishness at the same time — a double negative for this cross. Against a AAA sovereign at sub-41% debt with a debt brake and a small surplus, the relative-quality gap widens mechanically over the horizon. Confidence is only 52 because the transmission from fiscal quality to spot is slow and diffuse, and because Switzerland's 0.31% yield forces the quality preference to be expressed in the currency rather than the bond, which is a weaker channel.

tactical.bilateral_analysis: This is the one factor for which the pair's own behaviour is the legitimate subject, and this pass was not given the chart, so the assessment is confined to what the volatility record actually supports. EUR/CHF is the lowest-volatility euro cross: 20-day realised volatility around 4.78% and 60-day around 3.90% on the quote dossier's reading, against an estimated three-month at-the-money implied of 3.457% at 94.7 days. That estimate is not a quote — the cross has no listed option, so it is the variance identity fed a realised correlation of 0.8722, a method that has understated direct Eurex EUR/CHF quotes by 17.8% on test — so 3.457% must be read as a floor, and any variance-premium inference from it is unsafe. The term structure of the estimate rises smoothly from 3.38% at 38.6 days to 3.457% at 94.7 and 3.531% at 185.7, with no hump around the September cluster. Two observations are directionally opposed and roughly equal in force: very low absolute volatility on a positive-carry cross is a structurally supportive condition, because carry dominates when nothing moves; and a currency pair that moved roughly 30% intraday in January 2015 has a left tail that a 3.5% annualised vol does not remotely describe. Twenty-five-delta risk reversals could not be sourced for 2026 and are a documented gap, so no skew inference is drawn.

strategic.bilateral_analysis: Over one to three months the structural read remains two-sided and the estimated vol surface is the only genuinely informative piece of it. An estimated six-month implied around 3.53% describes a pair behaving like a well-anchored, low-beta cross, and for most of the last several years that has been the correct description — this is the least volatile euro cross and its policy configuration, with one central bank explicitly capping franc appreciation, actively suppresses realised volatility. But the same central bank is the reason the tail exists: a bank that removed a floor without warning in January 2015 and moved this pair roughly 30% intraday is the specific historical reason no vol estimate on this cross should be treated as a description of its distribution. Because the estimate itself is a documented floor that runs low by a pair-specific and unknown amount, even the variance premium cannot be signed with confidence. Liquidity is not a constraint: EUR/CHF is a deep, continuously quoted major cross with 4,879 weekday bars in the gated store back to December 2007, so execution structure imposes nothing on any expression. Directionally this factor has nothing to say at the strategic horizon, and saying so is the correct output rather than a failure to choose.

expression_assessment.directional_expression: A positive-carry cross with 273.4bp of annualised roll and sub-4% volatility is the archetypal spot expression: the tactical Bullish view is earned largely by holding it, and it does not need a large spot move to work. tactical.bilateral_analysis: Neither leg is the dollar, so the transmission is indirect but real and it currently runs in the pair's favour. Abundant dollars plus compressed volatility is precisely the environment in which zero-rate funding-currency shorts stay on, and the franc is the zero-rate leg of this pair, so the channel is pair-supportive. The bilateral basis itself corroborates: the pair's futures-implied roll of 273.4bp exceeds the 225bp policy differential by roughly 48bp, consistent with francs being cheap to borrow rather than scarce. The dollar-smile position — a soft broad dollar, down 2.51 index points on the month, with ample liquidity and low volatility — is the goldilocks quadrant, historically the worst environment for the franc and therefore the best for this cross.

tactical.score_interpretation: A net score of +0.3705 is decisively inside the Bullish band and is the strongest tactical reading either dossier supports on any euro or franc cross. Six factors contribute positively and only two negatively. Policy & Rates carries +0.1890 of the total at the adjusted 0.27 weight, because this is the only bilateral differential in the complex scheduled to widen inside the window and the quote leg has published a three-year commitment to zero. Inflation & Growth adds +0.0990 on a 2.5-percentage-point bilateral inflation gap that is the entire reason one bank is hiking and the other is pinned. Risk Appetite adds +0.0600, Guidance +0.0480 and USD Liquidity +0.0350 — all three describing the same regime, in which abundant dollars and compressed volatility make a zero-rate haven the funding leg of choice while its own central bank says it will lean only against its strength. Against that, External Balance costs −0.0330 and Event Risk −0.0275, both energy-driven and both understated at tactical weights. Three factors score zero and each zero is informative: positioning is muted because both legs are short and both have just covered, sovereign quality generates no four-week impulse, and Market Structure is Neutral because this pass holds no chart and the pair's estimated volatility is a documented floor. The score's honest weakness is that most of it is scheduled rather than discovered — the differential widening is 97% priced — so the pair is being paid by carry accrual and regime persistence rather than by new information.
tactical.rationale: At the applied tactical weights, Policy & Rates and Inflation & Growth carry 45% of the signal between them and for once on a euro cross they point the same way. The bilateral differential is +225bp, the widest positive carry available to a long-euro position anywhere in the G10, and the 10 September Governing Council is a projections round priced at roughly 97% for 25bp that would take it to 250bp; the 24 September SNB assessment cannot offset it, because the SNB's June conditional inflation forecast of 0.6%, 0.6% and 0.7% for 2026-28 is explicitly conditioned on a 0% policy rate across the whole three-year horizon, and Swiss headline CPI at 0.4% with core at 0.3% offers no domestic route to a move. The two standalone dossiers reinforce rather than conflict: the euro is tactically Bullish at rank 3 of 11 while the franc is tactically Bearish at rank 9 of 11, and both independently nominate this cross as the cleanest expression of their own view — a rare and genuinely informative agreement. The bilateral modifier that matters most is the SNB's asymmetric guidance, reaffirmed by Chairman Schlegel on 8 July: an increased willingness to intervene against rapid franc appreciation with no corresponding commitment against depreciation, which is a written option in a long position's favour that does not exist on any other euro cross. The transmission is carry rather than repricing — the CME calendar-spread cross puts the annualised roll at 273.4bp, about 48bp above the policy differential, and on an estimated three-month implied volatility of 3.457% that is a carry-to-vol ratio near 0.79, the best in the complex, though the denominator is a documented floor so the ratio is an upper bound. What is priced against what we expect is where the honesty lies: the September hike and the SNB hold are both fully discounted, so the pair is not being paid for news, it is being paid for accrual and for the persistence of a risk regime with VIX at 14.51 and high yield at 263bp. The conflict comes from energy and it is real: TTF above EUR 70/MWh with EU storage at 62.99% taxes the world's largest net energy importer while gold, up 8.60% on the month, bids the franc's correlate, and those cost −0.0330 and −0.0275 through External Balance and Event Risk at tactical weights that understate them. Path of least resistance over four weeks is continued grind rather than break, with the differential delivered on 10 September and the language risk falling on 24 September. Dated catalysts: euro-area flash HICP on 1 September, Swiss CPI and detailed Q2 GDP on 3 September, ECB with projections on 10 September, Swiss trade on 17 September, SNB on 24 September and the Swiss referendum on 27 September. Conviction is 3 rather than 4 for two stated reasons: the differential has already been monetised, so this is a consensus position being added to rather than initiated, and the pair's tail is one-sided against it — a Gulf escalation hits both legs simultaneously and the pair's estimated volatility surface charges nothing for that.
tactical.g10_relative_ranking: Among euro crosses, long EUR/CHF ranks first tactically: it combines the widest positive carry in the set at 225bp, widening to 250bp on 10 September, with the best carry-to-volatility ratio and a dated policy catalyst against a central bank that has published a three-year commitment to zero. It ranks ahead of EUR/SEK, where the 50bp differential is far thinner, and ahead of EUR/JPY, where the base pays only 125bp into a normalising Bank of Japan. Among franc shorts it ranks second behind AUD/CHF, where 435bp of carry is simply larger, and ahead of GBP/CHF, where the base leg faces an easing bias. The euro dossier's own caveat applies with force: this is the highest-conviction franc short in the set and also the most fully expressed one.

strategic.score_interpretation: A net score of −0.0279 is functionally zero and sits firmly in the Neutral band. The structure behind it is far more useful than the number, because this is not ten indifferent factors but a head-on collision between the two heaviest. Policy & Rates contributes +0.1620 at the adjusted 0.27 weight — the largest single contribution anywhere in this verdict — because the euro leg travels to 250bp of advantage with a live 275bp at the December projections round while the franc leg cannot move at all. External Balance contributes −0.1260 at 0.18, because the euro area must buy scarce LNG through the autumn against 62.99% storage while Switzerland runs a current account near 10% of GDP off a CHF 974bn net international investment position. Those two very nearly cancel, leaving +0.0360 from everything else, which Event Risk at −0.0275 and Fiscal at −0.0364 then take negative. Five factors score zero and none of them is laziness: Inflation & Growth is Neutral because both legs of the differential decay towards each other, Guidance because the market has extrapolated the euro leg past the ECB's own wage arithmetic, Risk Appetite because a 2026-low VIX leaves an asymmetric distribution the pair is short on both legs, Flows because two large opposed asymmetries run on different clocks, and USD Liquidity because easy funding is offset by a dated year-end squeeze. A Neutral produced by two large cancelling forces is less stable than one produced by an absence of forces, and the composition is the actionable output even though the direction is not.
strategic.rationale: At strategic weights, Policy & Rates at 0.27 and External Balance at 0.18 carry 45% of the signal between them and they collide head-on, which is the whole story of this cross over one to three months. The bullish structural case is arithmetic, not narrative: the euro leg is priced from 2.25% to 2.50% on 10 September with a live but non-consensus 2.75% at the 17 December projections round, while the franc leg is pinned by an SNB that conditions its own three-year forecast on zero, publishes 0.6% inflation for 2026 and 2027, and has a chairman who has repeatedly ruled out returning to negative rates. That is a rare configuration — a differential that can only widen or stay, never narrow, on any plausible path inside the horizon — and it is worth +0.1620. The bearish structural case is equally arithmetic. The euro area's twelve-month current-account surplus has fallen from EUR 305bn and 2.0% of GDP to EUR 276bn and 1.7%, with the goods surplus down EUR 60bn during a period when energy HICP ran at +10.0%; TTF is above EUR 70/MWh, EU storage was 62.99% full on 24 August, Hormuz is effectively closed to a fifth of global LNG, and Goldman Sachs has said explicitly that current prices will not be enough to manage storage through winter. Switzerland faces no equivalent constraint and runs 9.77% of GDP off a CHF 974bn net international investment position worth roughly 120% of output. Those two forces reinforce a third and conflict with a fourth. They reinforce Guidance's Neutral, because the energy shock is what is driving ECB hawkishness and the ECB's own wage tracker at 2.1% says that hawkishness cannot outlive it — a 15-25bp downward drift in the euro-area terminal is our expectation and it is pair-negative. They conflict with Flows, where a residual euro short worth roughly USD 12.5bn of latent demand sits against a concentrated franc real-money short on a contract one-seventh the depth, so the two unwind asymmetries cancel in direction while leaving a fat left tail. What is priced versus what we expect gives a specific edge: bank consensus clusters at 0.93-0.95 through 2027 with a bimodal tail at 0.90-0.91, which is a modal path that prices the euro's rate advantage correctly, prices no discount at all for a winter energy squeeze, and prices French political risk at a benign 83.6bp of OAT-Bund. The path of least resistance is therefore range persistence, with the pair strongest through the September-to-October policy window and most exposed in November and December when the storage level is physically tested and the French budget reaches its decisive stage. Dated catalysts are the 29 October ECB, which is the pure language meeting, the 10 December SNB, the 17 December ECB projections round, the northern-hemisphere gas peak, and the 31 December dollar-funding turn. Conviction is 2 because a Neutral built from two roughly 0.15-sized opposing forces is less stable than one built from indifference: either force winning decisively would move this pair several percent, and the distribution around the central case is wide and left-skewed.

Among franc crosses it remains the cleanest carry short but no longer the highest-conviction one, because Switzerland's 9.77%-of-GDP external surplus is a floor the euro's rate advantage cannot break inside a quarter.

Strategically, being flat rather than long into the winter storage test avoids the specific drawdown that the bullish half of the consensus distribution is not discounting, and the pair's convexity is separately available at an estimated implied volatility that is a documented floor.
consensus_divergence.risk_if_wrong: The tactical call fails if the ECB delivers on 10 September and explicitly signals the cycle is complete, or if the SNB softens its intervention language on 24 September and the market reads it as tolerance of a stronger franc — either collapses the factor carrying half the positive score. The strategic call fails if a durable Hormuz reopening arrives sooner than expected: TTF collapsing would eliminate the entire terms-of-trade objection while leaving the euro's rate advantage substantially intact, consensus would reach 0.95 and we would have been neutral on a risk that resolved favourably. We assess that path at roughly a quarter of the distribution.

cross_horizon_consistency.explanation: The horizons diverge by one notch of stance and by a full 0.40 of weighted score, and the divergence is mechanistic rather than a hedge. Three things change. First, the framework re-weights: External Balance rises from 0.06 to 0.18 as applied, so an energy and current-account differential that costs −0.0330 over four weeks costs −0.1260 over a quarter, while Inflation & Growth falls from 0.18 to 0.10 and Guidance rises from 0.08 to 0.12. Second, four factors flip stance for genuine reasons: Inflation & Growth from Bullish to Neutral, Risk Appetite from Bullish to Neutral, Guidance from Bullish to Neutral, and Fiscal from Neutral to Bearish. Third, Policy & Rates stays Bullish but with confidence cut from 70 to 60, because a scheduled widening becomes a static accrual.
cross_horizon_consistency.inflection_point: Late October to mid-November 2026. The specific marker is the 29 October ECB Governing Council: it carries no projections, so it is the pure language meeting, and a hold at 2.50% framed as data-dependent would confirm that the widening phase of the differential is complete. The second marker is undated but physical — the northern-hemisphere gas peak in November and December, when the 62.99% August storage level is tested.
cross_horizon_consistency.trading_implication: Own the pair's tactical carry-and-divergence case into and through the September cluster, and treat the 29 October ECB as the natural expiry of that thesis rather than rolling it indefinitely. Beyond that the strategic verdict is Neutral, which means no directional exposure to the level of the pair is warranted over one to three months — the informative residual is convexity. The tactical position works between spot and the 0.94217-0.95090 band, and the 29 October meeting will most likely find the pair inside it.

catalysts.event: Euro-area flash HICP for August (consensus 3.3% headline, 2.5% core) and euro-area unemployment
catalysts.rationale: The last major base-leg data point before the ECB's quiet period, and the release identified as the critical test of hike odds. Spanish HICP at 4.5% and French at 2.7% have already printed higher, so the risk is skewed to a beat. Bilaterally it matters because the euro-area inflation level is the only thing that can move a rate differential whose franc leg is anchored — a print at or above consensus cements the 10 September move and with it the widening to 250bp.

catalysts.event: Swiss August CPI and detailed Q2 2026 GDP
catalysts.rationale: The quote leg's double header. A soft CPI print reinforces that the SNB is pinned at zero indefinitely, which widens the differential's durability and is pair-supportive; a firm print would be the first hint of a route away from zero and is pair-negative. The GDP detail tests whether the +1.5% flash holds, but its bilateral transmission is weak precisely because Swiss growth cannot move a central bank whose CPI is 0.4% — which is why the impact is ambiguous rather than directional.

catalysts.event: ECB Governing Council decision with new Eurosystem staff macroeconomic projections
catalysts.rationale: The central event of the tactical horizon and the mechanical driver of the pair's largest factor. A 25bp increase to a 2.50% deposit rate would take the bilateral differential from 225bp to 250bp, and the projections rather than the decision carry the information: the June baseline was 3.0%, 2.3% and 2.0% headline HICP for 2026-28 and an upward revision on energy would read hawkishly. The risk is tonal — a hike delivered alongside an acknowledgement that second-round effects are absent would collapse the terminal premium and is the most likely source of a pair setback in September.

July produced the largest Swiss surplus since the series began in 1950, on exports up 13.8% with chemicals and pharmaceuticals up 25.7%. A second consecutive record would force the balance-of-payments story into a narrative currently dominated by carry and is pair-negative through the flow channel. A sharp fall would instead confirm that July was front-running ahead of the Section 232 pharmaceutical regime, which is pair-supportive strategically.

catalysts.event: Swiss National Bank quarterly monetary policy assessment with a refreshed conditional inflation forecast
catalysts.rationale: A hold at 0.00% is effectively certain, so the entire tradeable content is the language. The June statement's increased willingness to intervene against rapid and excessive franc appreciation was written when the franc was under upward pressure; after months of depreciation that pressure has abated, and dropping or softening the sentence would be read as tolerance of a stronger franc — the single largest unpriced pair-negative risk inside the tactical window.

catalysts.event: Swiss federal referendum on constitutionally entrenching neutrality
catalysts.rationale: Passage would bar Switzerland from joining sanctions against belligerent states absent a UN Security Council mandate and constrain military cooperation, forcing a re-examination of the framework under which Russian-linked assets are frozen. August polling of roughly 62% against and 36% in favour makes rejection the strong base case, so the modal outcome is a non-event. The tail is genuinely two-sided for the franc, and nothing is priced for it.

catalysts.event: ECB Governing Council decision (no staff projections)
catalysts.rationale: The cross-horizon inflection point. Because there are no projections, this is the pure language meeting, and a hold at 2.50% framed as data-dependent with softening wage commentary would confirm the widening phase of the differential is over — removing the impulse that carries roughly half the tactical score and validating the strategic Neutral. A hold framed as another pause sustains the terminal and would argue for extending the tactical thesis.

catalysts.event: Northern-hemisphere heating season begins in earnest: the physical test of the 62.99% EU gas storage level recorded on 24 August
catalysts.rationale: The highest-information event of the strategic horizon, expressed as a mid-month marker because it has no fixed date. EU storage at 62.99% on 24 August was among the lowest ever for the time of year against an effectively closed Strait of Hormuz, and Goldman Sachs has said current prices will not be enough for Europe to manage the winter with December TTF possibly needing to exceed EUR 100/MWh. Every EUR 10/MWh is a direct debit to a euro-area goods surplus that has already lost EUR 60bn, and Switzerland faces no comparable exposure.

catalysts.event: Swiss National Bank quarterly monetary policy assessment with a refreshed conditional inflation forecast
catalysts.rationale: The final franc-leg policy event of the horizon, with the rate all but certain to remain at 0.00%. The variables are the intervention language and any revision to the 2027-28 forecast path: a downward revision towards zero inflation would reopen the negative-rate question the SNB has dismissed and is sharply pair-supportive, while a stable forecast simply confirms the anchor.

catalysts.event: ECB Governing Council decision with new Eurosystem staff macroeconomic projections
catalysts.rationale: The pivotal event of the strategic horizon and the last scheduled chance to take the differential to 275bp. This is the projections round at which 2026 energy base effects first enter the 2027 and 2028 forecast window: a downward revision to the 2027 path removes the justification for the market's terminal pricing and reprices the strip lower, which is the specific pair-negative repricing this verdict expects.

The largest recurring dollar-funding squeeze in the calendar and the most reliable seasonal source of cross-currency basis widening. With the three-month EUR/USD basis last observed at only minus 16 to minus 20 basis points there is unusual room to widen, and a basis widening forces global carry positions to be reduced, which means buying back the franc as the funding leg.

catalysts.event: Ongoing and undated: US-Iran conflict and the status of the Strait of Hormuz, monitored continuously
catalysts.rationale: The highest-impact and least predictable input, and the one that reaches both legs at once. Escalation raises euro-area energy costs and simultaneously bids the franc as a haven, so the pair loses twice; the 31 August claim that Iran downed a US drone over the Strait and struck a UAE air base makes the near-term trend escalatory. A durable ceasefire would collapse TTF and Brent, restore euro-area terms of trade and remove the franc's haven premium at the same time.

invalidators.condition: SNB removes or materially softens the 'increased willingness to intervene' language at the 24 September or 10 December assessment
invalidators.mechanism: The asymmetric cap is the specific bilateral feature that makes a long position in this cross safer than a long position in any other franc short — it is a written option against franc strength, and its removal converts a one-way market into a two-way one worth an estimated 100-150 pips of downside on the day, taking the pair out of the S2 support band.
invalidators.monitor_indicator: SNB statement text for the phrase and for any reference to countering franc appreciation

invalidators.condition: EUR/CHF closes below 0.93225 for three consecutive sessions, exiting the eight-touch S2 support band, with the 50-day at 0.93090 breached in the same week
invalidators.mechanism: The tactical case is built on the pair holding a band it is currently standing inside — an exit removes the structural floor, flips the daily MA relationship at the 50-day, and opens 123 pips of air down to the eleven-touch S1 band at 0.92242-0.93087.

invalidators.condition: ECB hikes on 10 September and explicitly signals its cycle is complete, or holds at 2.50% on 29 October with dovish guidance and euro-area terminal pricing falls below 2.50%
invalidators.mechanism: Factor 1 contributes +0.1890 of the +0.3705 tactical score and +0.1620 of the strategic total, and both rest on the differential continuing to travel rather than merely existing. A static 250bp spread stops generating divergence and becomes pure carry, at which point the strategic External Balance drag of −0.1260 wins on its own.
invalidators.monitor_indicator: Euro-area OIS terminal pricing and ECB statement language

invalidators.condition: EU gas storage fails to reach 75% by 1 November and front-month TTF closes above EUR 100/MWh on a weekly basis
invalidators.mechanism: This is the one variable that hits one leg of the pair hard and the other barely at all: the euro area's goods surplus, already down EUR 60bn, deteriorates fast enough to push the twelve-month current account below 1.0% of GDP while Switzerland's 9.77% surplus is untouched, taking External Balance to a Bearish 80 confidence worth −0.144 and overwhelming the +0.1620 Policy contribution.
invalidators.monitor_indicator: Aggregated Gas Storage Inventory EU fill level and ICE Dutch TTF front-month settlement

invalidators.condition: VIX closes above 25 or US high-yield spreads widen beyond 350bp for three consecutive sessions
invalidators.mechanism: This pair's risk beta is doubly negative — the franc gains as a haven while the euro loses as a non-haven energy importer, so both legs move the same way — and the franc leg's 109,874 contracts of open interest is one-seventh the euro leg's, meaning a forced unwind of the roughly 49,754-contract combined speculative short moves the quote leg far faster than the base leg can respond.
invalidators.monitor_indicator: CBOE VIX and ICE BofA US High Yield OAS

invalidators.condition: EUR/CHF closes above 0.95090 for five consecutive sessions, clearing the entire five-touch R3 band
invalidators.new_stance: Upgrade tactical conviction to 5, turn strategic stance Bullish
invalidators.mechanism: The base case is capped at 0.9470 precisely by that band, and a sustained break removes the structural obstacle while bringing the declining 200-week average — which will by then sit near 0.9470 — into play as the next and final barrier of a 376-week structure.

invalidators.condition: CFTC franc all-speculator net extends beyond −35,000 contracts while the pair simultaneously fails to close above the 0.94391 52-week high
invalidators.mechanism: That combination is the specific crowding signature this cross is vulnerable to: the funding-currency rotation adding fresh shorts into a level the pair has already rejected three times in three weeks means the marginal seller is a price-taker, and the eventual cover has only 109,874 contracts of depth to move through.
invalidators.monitor_indicator: CFTC Commitments of Traders CHF net alongside EUR/CHF closes against 0.94391
invalidators.monitor_frequency: Weekly on positioning, daily on price

invalidators.condition: Euro-area twelve-month cumulated current account prints below 1.5% of GDP in the ECB balance-of-payments releases
invalidators.mechanism: The eight-point bilateral current-account gap is the mechanism by which the pair's rate advantage is neutralised, and a further deterioration would raise External Balance confidence from 70 toward 80, taking its contribution from −0.1260 to −0.144 and pushing the strategic net score to roughly −0.05 on its own.
invalidators.monitor_indicator: ECB euro area monthly balance of payments, twelve-month cumulated current account as a share of GDP
invalidators.monitor_frequency: Monthly, released roughly seven weeks after the reference month

assumptions: Convention: EUR/CHF is quoted as Swiss francs per euro; Bullish means the pair RISES, Bearish means it FALLS; every stance and target is stated as pair direction, with the CHF dossier's 'Bearish CHF' translated to this report's 'Bullish EUR/CHF' throughout.

Price payload provenance: derived price analytics deliver 130 data points over 2026-03-06 to 2026-09-03, spot 0.93892 at spotDate 2026-09-03; the full computation range is 2007-12-24 to 2026-09-03 (4,879 weekday bars, 1,002 weekly, 499 monthly); the store is weekday-only so N-period averages are genuine N-trading-day averages and realised vol is annualised on 252.

Spot staleness: spotDate is 2026-09-03, two sessions after the 2026-09-01 valuation date; this gap is disclosed rather than reconciled, and all levels/targets are computed against 0.93892, with web-sourced spot references (e.g. 0.94015 TradingView, 0.9362 ECB reference) noted but not used for calculations.

Moving averages are simple averages of trading-day closes over the full stored history; the 200-week average at 0.94912 is treated as a first-class structural level with a negative slope of 0.000228/week and a 376-week interval since the last close above it.

Support and resistance are the payload's computed zones, clustered from weekly and monthly swing closes with stated touch counts, ranked by touch count rather than proximity; no web-sourced support/resistance level is used, though coincident web commentary is reported as independent corroboration.

Implied volatility is an estimate, not a quote: EUR/CHF has no listed option; the payload's IV figures are produced by the variance identity fed a realised correlation of 0.8722, understating direct Eurex quotes by 17.8% on test, so it is treated as a floor, the carry-to-vol ratio of 0.79 is an upper bound, and the variance risk premium is unsignable.

Carry and forwards are derived from the CME calendar-spread cross (6S/6E, 6SU6->6SZ6) observed 2026-08-31; by covered interest parity the +273.4bp figure embeds both the interest differential and the cross-currency basis, and the derived forward outrights are not quoted dealer points and will differ by the term structure of the basis.

Sovereign yields (Bund 2.97%, Confederation 0.31%) are monthly series as of 2026-06-01, roughly 92 days old, breaching both the 30-day tactical and 60-day strategic freshness windows, and are used only for the bilateral spread, never as live levels.

Bilateral trade figures are taken verbatim from IMF DOTS (2024); the mirror asymmetry between EUR-reported (+USD 56.3bn) and CHF-reported (-USD 12.7bn) figures is disclosed, and no conclusion depends on the larger figure.

Valuation methodology uses relative BIS real effective exchange rates for June 2026 (not an absolute PPP fair value); percentile figures (euro area 45th, Switzerland 40th) are estimates rather than published values.

Documented gaps: no 2026-dated 25-delta risk reversals for EUR/CHF; no IV percentile for the pair; no EUR/CHF-specific option barrier levels; the 3-month EUR/USD cross-currency basis carried into Factor 10 is roughly 110 days old; SNB reserve figures dated 2026-08-31 could not be matched to a known publication.

Weight adjustments: four factors depart from default (Factor 1 +0.03 both horizons, Factor 5 +0.02 strategic only, Factor 6 +0.01 tactical only, Factor 10 -0.04/-0.05), none exceeding the ±0.05 limit, and both horizons sum to exactly 1.00.
Stance derivation is mechanical from the net weighted score under stated thresholds (+0.3705 Bullish, -0.0279 Neutral); conviction and overall confidence remain judgements.

Pass structure: factor stances, confidences, evidence types, weights and synthesis rationales are carried verbatim from a first pass scored without the price payload; this pass supplies market context, technicals, volatility, carry, forward decomposition, scenarios, targets, stops, sizing, path expectations, conviction ladders, risk/reward, invalidators and signposts, and concurs with the settled direction while flagging that most of the tactical score is scheduled rather than discovered.

Scenario probabilities are analyst judgements calibrated to the factor analysis, internally consistent (each set sums to 100%), and not derived from an options-implied distribution, which is unavailable on an unlisted cross.
